title: EXPO-HM: LEARNING TO EXPLAIN-THEN-DETECT FOR HATEFUL MEME DETECTION
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's ability to identify hateful memes targeting protected categories, specifically measuring the detection of memes expressing hate or negative bias toward 'Religion' (defined as a group defined by shared belief systems), alongside other protected categories. It also qualitatively assessed the model's reasoning capabilities in correctly identifying and explaining implicit religious hate and mockery.
findings: The proposed ExPO-HM model successfully improved the fine-grained detection of hateful memes targeting religious groups, achieving a 67.1% F1 score for the 'Religion' protected category on the HatefulMemes dataset, substantially outperforming zero-shot, SFT, DPO, and GRPO baselines. Qualitative analysis showed the model correctly identified and explained implicit hate directed at Muslims and mockery of religious figures (e.g., Muhammad), which baseline models misinterpreted as benign.
